Rashi on Chullin 11a:1:1.hebrew: כגון דקיימי דרא דגברי - האחד עומד במפתן ורואה, ומגיד לזה, וזה לזה, עד הכהן, דלא בציר:
Rashi on Chullin 11a:1:1.english: Such as where there is a row of men standing - One of them stands at the threshold [of the house under quarantine] and sees [the mark], and tells the one next to him, and that one tells the next, until it reaches the priest, provided that [the row] has no gap in it.

Rashi on Chullin 11a:2:1.english: From where [do we know] this matter - Since [the Gemara] was dealing with [the phrase] "from where [do we know] this matter" regarding a chazakah [presumptive status], it also stated this one here.

Rashi on Chullin 11a:2:2.english: From where do we [derive] this - [This is stated] as a question.

Rashi on Chullin 11a:3:1.hebrew: תשע חנויות - כולן מוכרות בשר שחוטה ואחת מוכרת בשר נבלה, ונמצא בשר בארץ, הלך אחר הרוב, דהא קמן חזינא דרובא דהיתירא:
Rashi on Chullin 11a:3:1.english: Nine stores - All of them sell [kosher] slaughtered meat, and one sells the meat of a carcass [neveilah], and [some] meat is found lying on the ground - one follows the majority, for here we plainly see that the majority is permitted.

Rashi on Chullin 11a:3:2.english: And Sanhedrin - As we learned [in a mishna] (Sanhedrin 40a): [If] twelve [judges] vote to acquit and eleven vote to convict, [the defendant] is acquitted.

Rashi on Chullin 11a:4:1.hebrew: קטן וקטנה - דפליגי רבנן עליה דר"מ ביבמות (דף סא:), דתנן: יבם קטן שבא על יבמה קטנה, יגדלו זה עם זה, ולא חיישינן שמא תמצא אילונית או הוא סריס, ונמצא פוגע באשת אחיו שלא במקום מצוה, דבעי להקים לאחיו שם, והאי לאו בר הכי הוא, אלא אמרינן זיל בתר רוב קטנים דעלמא דאינם סריסים, והיינו רובא דליתיה קמן:
Rashi on Chullin 11a:4:1.english: A minor boy and a minor girl - Because the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Meir in Yevamot (page 61b), where we learned: [If] a minor levir had relations with a minor yevama, they should grow up together, and we are not concerned lest she turn out to be an aylonit (infertile) or he a saris (impotent), such that he would be improperly engaging with his brother's wife not for the sake of the mitzvah - since [the mitzvah] requires establishing offspring in his brother's name, and this one would not be capable of that - rather, we say: follow the majority of minors in the world generally, who are not sterile, and this is a case of "a majority not present before us."

Tosafot on Chullin 11a:1:1.hebrew: דקיימי דרא דגברי - בלא זה היה יכול לומר, כגון שהיה אדם אחד עומד לשם בשעת הסגר וראה שלא חסר; אלא רוצה לפרש באותו ענין, שאף הכהן עצמו היה יכול לידע:
Tosafot on Chullin 11a:1:1.english: That a row of men were standing - Without this, he could have said, for example, that a single man was standing there at the time of the quarantine (hesger) and saw that it did not diminish; rather, he wishes to explain [the matter] in that same fashion, that even the kohen himself could have known [it].

Tosafot on Chullin 11a:2:1.hebrew: מנא הא מילתא דאמור רבנן זיל בתר רובא - וא"ת: כיון דאמרינן זיל בתר חזקה, כ"ש בתר רובא, דרובא וחזקה - רובא עדיף. וי"ל: דלרב אחא בר יעקב בעי, דלא קים ליה חזקה מקרא. ולמאי דמפרש רבינו חיים, דהא דרובא עדיף מחזקה לא מסברא, אלא ילפינן מפרה אדומה, דאזלינן בתר רובא אע"ג דאיכא חזקה כנגד הרוב, דאוקי גברא שמזין עליו בחזקת טמא, אתי שפיר הכא:
Tosafot on Chullin 11a:2:1.english: From where do we know this matter, that the Rabbis said, "Follow the majority" - And if you should say: Since we say, "follow the presumption (chazakah)," how much more so should we follow the majority (rov), for between majority and presumption, the majority is preferable. And one can say: this [question] applies according to Rav Acha bar Yaakov, for he does not hold that the presumption itself is derived from a verse. And according to what Rabbeinu Chaim explains - that the majority's superiority over the presumption is not [known] from logic, but rather we derive it from [the law of] the red heifer (parah adumah), that we follow the majority even though there is a presumption opposing the majority, in that we establish the man upon whom they sprinkle [its waters] as having a presumption of impurity - this fits well here.
